guided.title: Clean a name column
guided.prompt: Create the Series `names` by stripping the spaces and applying title case to `df["name"]`. Print the list of cleaned names on line 1 and, on line 2, the number of distinct names before and after cleaning separated by a space.
guided.starter:
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)

df = pd.DataFrame({"name": ["  ana SILVA", "Bob king ", "CY lopez", "ana silva"], "email": ["Ana@Shop.com", "bob@shop.COM", "cy@mail.org", "ana@shop.com"]})
guided.solution:
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)

names = df["name"].str.strip().str.title()

guided.title: Test and filter
guided.prompt: Print the list of emails (lower-cased) whose domain ends with `.com` (use `str.lower()` then `str.endswith`) on line 1 and the number of emails that contain `shop` regardless of case on line 2 (`str.contains(..., case=False)`).

guided.title: Extract a pattern
guided.prompt: From `codes`, extract the digits after `ORD-` as one column using `str.extract` with the pattern `ORD-(\d+)`, convert them to numbers with `pd.to_numeric`, and print the list. Then print the number of codes that did not match.
guided.starter:
import pandas as pd

codes = pd.Series(["ORD-0042", "ORD-7", "INV-100", "ORD-310"])
guided.solution:
import pandas as pd

codes = pd.Series(["ORD-0042", "ORD-7", "INV-100", "ORD-310"])
num = codes.str.extract(r"ORD-(\d+)")[0]
print(pd.to_numeric(num).tolist())
print(int(num.isna().sum()))
hints: `extract` returns a DataFrame; column 0 is the first capture group.
Non-matching rows give `NaN`; `to_numeric` keeps `NaN` as it is.

independent.title: Clean a customer table
independent.prompt: Clean `raw` into `clean` without changing `raw`: strip each customer name, lower-case it, and replace double spaces by a single space (`str.replace("  ", " ", regex=False)`), then title-case it; convert `spend` to numbers by removing `$` and `,` (regular expression `[$,]` with `regex=True`) and using `to_numeric(errors="coerce")`. Print `clean`, then the sorted distinct customer names (missing excluded) as a list, then the total spend and the number of missing spend values.
independent.starter:
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)

raw = pd.DataFrame({"customer": [" ana silva", "BOB KING", "Ana  Silva", None, "bob king "],
                    "spend": ["$1,250.50", "$300", "n/a", "$45.25", "$1,000"]})
independent.solution:
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)

raw = pd.DataFrame({"customer": [" ana silva", "BOB KING", "Ana  Silva", None, "bob king "],
                    "spend": ["$1,250.50", "$300", "n/a", "$45.25", "$1,000"]})
clean = raw.assign(
    customer=raw["customer"].str.strip().str.lower().str.replace("  ", " ", regex=False).str.title(),
    spend=pd.to_numeric(raw["spend"].str.replace(r"[$,]", "", regex=True), errors="coerce"),
)
print(clean)
print(sorted(clean["customer"].dropna().unique().tolist()))
print(clean["spend"].sum(), int(clean["spend"].isna().sum()))
independent.expected:
customer    spend
0  Ana Silva  1250.50
1   Bob King   300.00
2  Ana Silva      NaN
3       None    45.25
4   Bob King  1000.00
['Ana Silva', 'Bob King']
2595.75 1

independent.title: Parse a log column
independent.prompt: The `log` column holds entries such as `2024-03-05 ERROR disk full`. Without dates (those are for a later day), use `str.split(" ", n=2, expand=True)` to build a table with the columns `day`, `level` and `message`. Print that table, then the number of ERROR entries (a mask on `level`), then the list of messages of the ERROR entries, then the number of entries whose message contains `disk` (any case).
independent.starter:
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)

log = pd.Series(["2024-03-05 ERROR disk full", "2024-03-05 INFO started", "2024-03-06 ERROR Disk read failed", "2024-03-07 WARN slow response"])
independent.solution:
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)

log = pd.Series(["2024-03-05 ERROR disk full", "2024-03-05 INFO started", "2024-03-06 ERROR Disk read failed", "2024-03-07 WARN slow response"])
parsed = log.str.split(" ", n=2, expand=True)
parsed.columns = ["day", "level", "message"]
print(parsed)
errors = parsed["level"] == "ERROR"
print(errors.sum())
print(parsed.loc[errors, "message"].tolist())
print(parsed["message"].str.contains("disk", case=False).sum())

day  level           message
0  2024-03-05  ERROR         disk full
1  2024-03-05   INFO           started
2  2024-03-06  ERROR  Disk read failed
3  2024-03-07   WARN     slow response
2
['disk full', 'Disk read failed']
2

independent.title: Validate and extract codes
independent.prompt: The codes below should look like `AB-1234-XY` (two capital letters, four digits, two capital letters). Use `str.extract` with named groups `prefix`, `num` and `suffix` to build a table, print it, print how many codes are invalid (rows where `num` is missing) and print the sum of the valid numbers as an integer (convert with `to_numeric` and use `sum`).
independent.starter:
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)

codes = pd.Series(["AB-1234-XY", "CD-0042-ZZ", "bad", "EF-99-QQ", "GH-7000-KL"])
independent.solution:
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 20)

codes = pd.Series(["AB-1234-XY", "CD-0042-ZZ", "bad", "EF-99-QQ", "GH-7000-KL"])
out = codes.str.extract(r"(?P<prefix>[A-Z]{2})-(?P<num>\d{4})-(?P<suffix>[A-Z]{2})")
print(out)
print(int(out["num"].isna().sum()))
print(int(pd.to_numeric(out["num"]).sum()))
independent.expected:
prefix   num suffix
0     AB  1234     XY
1     CD  0042     ZZ
2    NaN   NaN    NaN
3    NaN   NaN    NaN
4     GH  7000     KL
2
8276

checks.question: What does `s.str.strip()` do to the Series `s`?
options: Returns a new Series; `s` is unchanged unless you store the result
Raises an error on a Series
checks.explanation: String methods in the accessor return a new Series. The result must be stored for the change to last.

checks.question: What does `pd.Series(["Ab", None]).str.lower().tolist()` return?
checks.explanation: Missing values stay missing instead of raising an error or becoming the text none.

checks.question: Why use `na=False` in `s.str.contains("x", na=False)` before using it as a filter?
options: A mask with missing values cannot be used for filtering; `na=False` turns gaps into False
checks.explanation: For missing cells `contains` returns a missing value, and a mask with missing values raises an error. `na=False` makes those rows simply not match.

checks.question: What does `pd.Series(["a b", "c d"]).str.split(" ").str[1].tolist()` return?
checks.explanation: `split` gives a list per row and `.str[1]` picks item 1 of each list, the second word.

checks.question: What does `pd.Series(["SKU-12", "x"]).str.extract(r"SKU-(\d+)")[0].tolist()` return?
checks.explanation: `extract` returns only the capture group, as text, and `NaN` for rows that do not match. The digits are still text until converted with `to_numeric`.

checks.question: What does `"ana" in df["name"]` test?
options: Whether `ana` is one of the index labels
Whether all names start with ana
checks.explanation: `in` on a Series looks in the index, like a dictionary. Use `df["name"].str.contains("ana").any()` to test the text.
